title.narrative: BBCMA Stärka en generation av unga kambodjaner 2021-2023

description.narrative:
BBCMA's Klahan9 SPACE project's main objective is to increase levels of civic engagement among young people in Cambodia by "equipping them with the knowledge, skills, confidence, motivation and networks to participate and enhancing conditions for them to do so". The following are anticipated outcomes of the project:
Outcome 1: Young women and men have improved knowledge on civic issues and ways to participate in public life
Outcome 2: Young women and men have increased skills, confidence, motivation and networks to participate in public life
Outcome 3: Young women and men have sustained opportunities to express themselves and engage in constructive dialogue and discussion on public issues
Outcome 4: More positive attitudes towards young women and mens participation in public life are held by parents, community gatekeepers and decision-makers
The hypothesis of the proposal is that at the end of the implementation of the programme each individual will be impacted by the anticipated outcomes, and that individual and collective efforts with the aim to increase levels of civic engagement could make a difference in the civic life of one's community and developing the combination of knowledge, skills, values and motivation to make a more enabling environment in Cambodian society.

Det nuvarande projektet sedan 2021 som pågår till 2024 med titeln "Klahan9 SPACE - Stimulating participation and civic engagement" avser att ta itu med vanliga kunskaper, attitydmässiga och kompetensrelaterade hinder för deltagande samt positivt förändra sociala och kulturella normer som hindrar unga människors deltagande i det offentliga livet baserat på resultaten av deras informerade forskningsstudier.
Projektet syftar till att stärka en generation av unga kambodjaner genom att stimulera deltagande och samhällsengagemang. Klahan9 SPACE kommer att ge unga kvinnor och män möjlighet att delta i beslutsfattandet om samhällsfrågor som påverkar dem och deras samhällen, genom att skapa inkluderande online- och offlineutrymmen för engagemang och förstärka deras röster. Unga kvinnor och män kommer att utrustas med kunskap, färdigheter och självförtroende för att engagera sig och påverka beslutsfattandet i frågor som är viktiga för dem och deras samhällen. Detta kommer att ske genom att förändra negativa normer och attityder kring ungdomars deltagande, uppmuntra diskussioner med beslutsfattare och stärka tillgången till medier av allmänt intresse för och som representerar ungdomar.

The current project since 2021 lasting until 2024 entitled “Klahan9 SPACE – Stimulating participation and civic engagement” intends to address common knowledge, attitudinal and skills-related barriers to participation as well as positively shifting social and cultural norms which inhibit young people’s participation in public life based on the findings of their informed research studies.
The project aims at empowering a generation of young Cambodians through stimulating participation and civic engagement. Klahan9 SPACE will empower young women and men to participate in decision making on civic issues that affect them and their communities, creating inclusive online and offline spaces for engagement and amplifying their voices. Young women and men will be equipped with knowledge, skills and self-efficacy to engage and influence decision-making on issues that matter to them and their communities. This will be done by shifting negative norms and attitudes around youth participation, encouraging discussions, with decision-makers and strengthening the provision of public interest media for and representative of youth.

The SPACE projects innovative approach, consisting of four interconnected workstreams or 'pillars' (media production, community outreach, media support and training, and research), successfully engaged a diverse range of youth, including those from historically underserved communities.
Over the course of its implementation the project has made significant progress in reaching its target beneficiaries, over 2.46 million people aged 15-55 including 1.14 million young people aged 15-30, across diverse demographics such as gender, location, and education level. The project has successfully achieved its intended objectives, with the final project evaluation demonstrating growth across all outcome indicators, which are also reflected at the impact level.
The SPACE project has played a crucial role in promoting civic engagement and empowering a new generation of young Cambodians to participate in public life, despite the overall shrinking civic space in Cambodia due to restrictions on freedom of expression and barriers to youth participation. The evaluation shows a statistically significant increase in youth civic participation, rising from 55% in 2020 to 64% in 2024.
The overall increase in participation was most prominent among young people highly exposed to the projects media outputs and outreach initiatives. A significant rise in female participation was also observed, increasing from 47% at baseline to 60% at endline, while male participation saw a more modest increase from 58% to 61%. This highlights a notable shift toward gender equality in youth civic engagement, with female youth making more substantial gains.
Young people's understanding of how to engage in civic life has been enhanced through tools like accountability boxes, volunteering, and community meetings. Exposure to the project increased young people's ability to identify ways to help their community (36% vs. 23% for those not exposed) and boosted motivation to participate in civic activities (from 6% in 2020 to 23% in 2024). Confidence in public discussions, community meetings, and volunteering also rose by 13% (from 14% to 27%), demonstrating that the project achieved its overall outcomes.
Examples of results under the respective pillar:
The Media Content Production under the SPACE program, including TV programs and digital content, has informed Cambodian youth about key issues in their lives and inspired them to take action in support of their communities' development. Carefully tailored to audience needs, the content aimed to challenge negative social norms while exploring feasible individual and collective actions within their environment. In 2024, a total of 256 social media content pieces were produced and distributed on Klahan9s widely followed platforms, including 98 pieces under the leaving no one behind theme. With a creative approach to engagement, this content received 22M reaches and generated 1.5M engagements on the Klahan9 Facebook page. The 33 episodes of the TV drama were repeatedly broadcast weekly on the TV channel, reaching 2 million viewers.
The Community Outreach Component has meant that BBCMA and project partners used a range of approaches, including delivering Roadshow Academy events in schools; establishing youth forums for young people to engage with parents, community leaders and policymakers on key issues; and conducting youth network meetings where young people could share knowledge and learning with their peers. Community outreach interventions delivered by BBC Media Action and its partners under the SPACE program in 2024 directly engaged more than 3,700 young people (2,300 women and 34 LGBTQ), enhancing their knowledge and motivation for civic participation. These initiatives also created opportunities for young people, parents, local authorities, and NGOs to interact, exchange perspectives, and build mutual understanding - fostering a more supportive environment for youth engagement in civic life.
The Media Support made sure that BBC Media Action also provided media capacity-strengthening workshops and online courses for journalists, NGOs, and media outlets, enhancing the production of high-quality public interest content. This includes the work to support 22 female journalists from the Cambodian Female Journalists (CFJ) network whose work focuses on gender equality in the media sector. These efforts contributed to improved media literacy, critical thinking, and the fight against misinformation, ultimately fostering greater youth participation in civic life. In 2024, the SPACE media support workstream successfully empowered young media practitioners, journalists, and content creators to amplify youth voices and promote civic engagement. Through partnerships with local media, 46 young media practitioners - including 25 women, 1 indigenous youth, and 4 LGBTQI individuals - produced 449 media pieces on youth issues, reaching 5.5 million users via social media and online platforms.
The Research Component has continuously helped to to capture crucial insights and learning that supported the project's improvement and enhanced understanding of the project impact on its audience as a whole. Since 2024 was a critical year for concluding the results of project implementation, the research component made a strong investment in conducting a comprehensive endline evaluation. This included a diverse range of research techniques, methodologies, and innovations - such as randomized controlled trial (RCT) and impact story collection - complementing broader surveys and qualitative research. Extensive research and data collection efforts were carried out to ensure robust evidence for assessing the project's success, challenges, lessons learned, and areas for improvement, shaping the direction of future project implementation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
